source_checks.finding: Page confirmed for iPhone. Excerpt matches the page exactly: 'If you can't connect to Wi-Fi, then check your Wi-Fi settings or troubleshoot network issues.' The page says open the Settings app, make sure Wi-Fi is turned on, tap the network name to join, look for a blue checkmark, make sure Airplane Mode is off, make sure Connectivity Assist is off, restart the device if the Wi-Fi setting appears dimmed (grayed out), and that if you still see a message like 'No Internet Connection' there might be another issue, then check your router and network settings.

Android-only page; scope confirmed. Distractor for this iPhone user, correctly not used in the target. Excerpt matches the page exactly: 'If you can't access the Internet on your Android device, either through an app or a website, try these troubleshooting steps.'

Make sure Connectivity Assist is off
If the Wi-Fi setting is dimmed, restart the device
If No Internet Connection still shows, check the router and network settings

findings: Step 3 'Tap the name of the network you want to join' repeats a step the user has already done. The user reports full Wi-Fi bars, so the phone is already on the network.
Step 5 begins 'If you still can't connect', but the user is connected and sees 'No Internet Connection', so the condition does not match the user's situation.
Step 6 combines two actions: checking that Connectivity Assist is off and restarting the device if the Wi-Fi setting is dimmed.
correction_required: Delete step 3 and renumber. Change step 5 to 'Return to Settings and make sure Airplane Mode is off.' Split step 6 into 'Tap Wi-Fi again and make sure Connectivity Assist is off.' and a separate step 'If the Wi-Fi setting is dimmed, restart the device.' Keep the router and network settings check as the final step.
